title: Fix cache metric double-counting on streaming retries
author: Samir Qureshi
description:
Context: After landing the new KV/prefix cache telemetry counters, we noticed inflated hit/miss totals on routes with streaming enabled when the gateway/runtime triggers a stream retry (e.g., transient upstream disconnect mid-stream). The retry path replays the same logical request, but we were emitting request-scoped cache counters on both the initial attempt and the retry attempt, effectively double counting a single user request. This shows up as a hit-rate dip and a spikes in wasted_prefill for retry-heavy windows.

Root cause: The streaming pipeline creates a new internal attempt for a retry while keeping the same external request identity. Our cache metrics emission was wired to the stream finalizer callback, which can run for both the aborted attempt and the successful retry attempt. Since the cache metrics are intended to be attributed to the logical request (not per attempt), we must ensure emission is idempotent across retries.

Fix: Add an explicit per-logical-request emission guard in the streaming request context. We track a single "cache_metrics_emitted" bit on the logical request context, shared across attempts. The abort path no longer emits request-level cache counters; only the attempt that transitions the logical request to terminal success/failure emits counters once, with retry attribution recorded via tracing annotation (low-cardinality) rather than metrics labels.

Retry semantics note (agreed w/ SRE + Telemetry): For cache efficiency metrics (hit/miss, reuse, wasted_prefill), a gateway/runtime retry should be treated as a single logical request to avoid penalizing noisy networks. We still want visibility into retry rate separately (existing request retry metrics + trace events), but cache metrics should not double count.

What changes:
- Ensure KV/prefix cache counters/histograms are emitted at most once per logical request even when streaming retries occur.
- Add a regression test that forces a mid-stream retry and asserts counters increment exactly once.
- Add a trace annotation "cache.telemetry.skipped_due_to_retry_abort" when an attempt aborts before metrics emission (for debugging).

Test plan:
- New unit/regression test: simulated streaming retry (abort attempt #1, complete attempt #2) and assert: (1) hit/miss counters increment once, (2) wasted_prefill increments once, (3) no duplicate per-request finalization.
- Local: run runtime tests + streaming integration suite.
- Perf: no additional per-token overhead; the guard is a single atomic bool on request context.

Rollout: Safe to backport if needed; behavior change is only to prevent overcounting. Dashboards/alerts should stabilize (no more false hit-rate dips correlated with retry spikes).

Related: PRs #18421, #18424, #18430; Slack thread eng-runtime/1740422218-fix-double-counting-on-stream-retries.
commits: runtime/streaming: make cache metrics emission idempotent across retries
runtime/telemetry: skip request-level cache counters on aborted stream attempt
tests: add streaming retry regression test for cache metrics
tracing: annotate aborted attempts to aid debugging without new metric labels
changed_files: runtime/src/streaming/stream_session.rs (share logical request context across attempts; add cache_metrics_emitted guard)
runtime/src/telemetry/cache_metrics.rs (move emission to logical terminalization; avoid abort emission)
runtime/src/telemetry/streaming.rs (trace annotation for abort path; small refactor for clarity)
conversation:
Omar El-Sayed (review): Can you clarify whether we want to count cache metrics per attempt or per logical request? For perf investigations, per-attempt could be useful, but dashboards will get messy.
Samir Qureshi (author): Agreed. For the new cache efficiency set, we decided per logical request (aligns w/ ADR language and SRE expectations). Per-attempt is better captured via tracing; I added a trace event on abort so we can still correlate retries w/ cache behavior.

Nadia Rahman (review): Please avoid adding any retry-related label to the cache metrics; we can’t afford the cardinality risk. Also, make sure aborted attempts don’t emit partial histograms (those are hard to reason about).
Samir Qureshi: Done. No labels added. Abort path no longer emits any cache counters/histograms. Only the terminal attempt emits, guarded by cache_metrics_emitted.

Noah Patel (review): Is the guard thread-safe? We’ve had weird double-finalize behavior with streaming sessions under cancellation.
Samir Qureshi: Guard is an AtomicBool on the logical request context. Both cancel and retry paths call into finalize; we now do a compare_exchange to ensure single emission.

Omar (request changes): The regression test should cover: (a) abort + retry + success, and (b) abort + retry + abort (terminal failure). We’ve seen both.
Samir: Added the second case and asserts that emission still happens exactly once for the final terminalization (failure).

All reviewers approved after updates.
release_notes: - Fix: Prevent double-counting prefix/KV cache metrics when streaming retries occur (cache hit/miss, reuse, wasted_prefill). Clarifies retry attribution: cache efficiency metrics are per logical request; retry visibility remains in request retry metrics and traces.
